newsitem.title: USA: US debt futures end firm, propped by budget hopes.
newsitem.headline: US debt futures end firm, propped by budget hopes.

text.p: U.S. debt futures rallied strongly on U.S. jobs data early, cut gains and languished most of the day, but recovered late to close mid-range.
Traders tied the late bid to speculation that a U.S. budget agreement was at hand.

Late in the session, White House officials said Republicans and the administration were close to announcing an agreement to balance the federal budget by 2002. President Clinton said he hoped to be able to comment "one way or the other" soon. After the close, a senior administration official said a deal had been struck.
U.S. stocks rallied late and U.S. June T-bonds drifted up to resistance at 109-28/32 to 30/32 on the budget hopes. Traders said action was light overall.

"It looks like the bond did pretty well at the end of the day here, based on thoughts about a budget deal," said Kurt Fraim, futures analyst with Aubrey G. Lanston. "That was the key thing for the last two hours of trade," he said.
He noted an underlying firm tone across the yield curve, and said strength tied to the budget news could persist into early next week.
Still, he noted a quarterly refunding looms next week.
Early trading was very choppy and volume brisk as traders scrambled to assess the jobs data.

Initially, June T-bonds rallied to a two month high at 110-10/32 as traders keyed off of weaker than expected April jobs growth. Jobs rose 142,000 compared with a 211,000 trade consensus and a downwardly revised 139,000 in March.
But the focus soon switched to the drop in the jobless rate, which fell to 4.9 percent from 5.2 percent, the lowest level in 23 years.
Futures cut gains and listless trade ensued with prices tethered close to Thursday's closing levels.
Traders and technicians said the market just ran out of steam after a week of solid gains.
"It's been a week of unemployment days," one Eurodollar trader said of the data-filled week.
They said the market would stabilize and trade in a range short-term, particularly since June T-bonds rallied above 110-2/32 to 3/32, the 50-percent retracement of the February 18 to April 11 break.
One technician pegged a likely range from 108-20/32 to 110-17/32.

At the close, June T-bonds were up 8/32 at 109-29/32, 10-year notes rose 3/32 to 107-8/32, September T-bills were up 0.10 at 94.470, September Eurodollars were flat at 93.885 and December Eurodollars were 0.025 higher at 93.680. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
